newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French, German stocks hit peak on Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French, German stocks hit peak on Wall St.

text.p: German and French shares struck record highs on Monday, bolstered by Wall Street's fourth high of the year on Friday.
Tokyo shares also staged a sharp rebound following a torrid few days last week and the London stock market joined the other major European equity markets with strong early gains.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar held steady in early European trade after shrugging off the 4.7 percent rally in Japanese stocks overnight.
Sterling slipped following subdued British output prices for December, which eased speculation about a possible rise in interest rates this week.
Wall Street's rebound to a record close on Friday provided the impetus needed to push the Paris bourse to a trading record of 2,370.87 on the CAC-40 index.
This surpassed the previous trading peak of 2,360.98 set in February 1994 and underlined the recent strength of the French market, which has lagged its main European rivals for more than a year.
The leading index was up more than 1.7 percent by 1055 GMT.

"The bourse is swept up by Wall Street, by the bond markets and by expectations of higher corporate results in France for 1997," said Jean-Pierre Filbien, director of sales at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Paris.
However, Pierre Amancic of IFF Bourse said he saw a risk of an abrupt correction after such a rapid rise.
"The indicators are signalling that the market's overbought. There's a risk of a violent retracement that could take us back as far as 2,200 points."
Among the biggest gainers was luxury goods group LVMH, which rose 2.27 percent after announcing on Saturday it had completed the acquisition of duty free chain DFS.

Carmaker Renault rose more than three percent to 112 francs after chairman Louis Schweitzer told the newspaper Figaro he expected the car operation to show a bigger loss in 1996 but aimed to break even in 1997.
German shares also opened bourse trade at record highs, following Wall Street higher and supported by the strength of the dollar and the German debt market.
Dealers said that provided there were no shocks in U.S. comsumer price data on Tuesday, the 30-share DAX index could test 3,000 points.
The DAX touched a record of 2,958.38 after the IBIS-DAX also struck a new high in pre-bourse electronic trade. The DAX later slipped slightly to 2,956.38 for a net gain of nearly 23 points.
Deutsche Telekom underperformed the market as initial analyst stock recommendations began to emerge. The stocks was off slightly at 30.70 marks.
London stocks also took their lead from Wall Street, the FTSE 100 index rising one percent in early trade to show a 40 point gain at 4,097.
Dealers noted the sharp recovery in Tokyo and said fears of an imminent rise in British interest rates had waned after signs that consumer spending has been less robust than expected over Christmas.
Even as the FTSE pushed back towards the 4,123.2 record set on December 31, some traders said the extreme volatility in international stock markets could be a restraining factor.
"The markets seem to have gone haywire," said the head of equity sales at one top investment bank. "Whether this is the final topside blow-off we've been expecting I don't know."
Foreign exchange analysts said the dollar outlook remained bullish amid growing speculation of higher U.S. rates in the near term, particularly after Friday's strong U.S. jobs data.
"The widening U.S.-German 10-year yield spread is providing a high return over Germany, leaving the dollar with pretty decent support," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1045 GMT
The dollar was trading at 116.29 yen and 1.5836 marks compared with 115.96 and 1.5855 late in Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1045 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was up 40.6 points, or 1.0 percent, at 4,097.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 40.54 points, or 1.74 percent, at 2,368.04.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 22.99 points, or 0.78 percent, at 2,956.38.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $359.60 against $358.25 on Friday. Silver was unchanged at $4.77.
